0.reason: the launch==cli gate is uncovered by a negative case; the behaviour is right and a covering case is a test addition, not a landing blocker

1.reason: a duplicated session predicate beside _launched_prior_session; sharing it is a reuse cleanup that changes no behaviour

findings.text: the launch == "cli" gate is load-bearing — it is what keeps an in-harness run, whose session id is its coordinator's own, from being read alive by any live process carrying that id — and no case covers it: all five cases write launch "cli" (tests/test_resume_finds_unrecorded_live_session.py:174), so deleting the gate leaves the suite green and the in-harness false positive undetected

the whole-element session test is restated here rather than shared with its owner _launched_prior_session (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:545), which the plan named as the predicate to call; an argv-level predicate owned by that module and called from both sites would keep one definition of "this launch carries this session"

the read can only see a resumed worker, because the id enters argv only in the resume dialect (reckon/_backends.py:1682 and reckon/_backends.py:1335); a freshly launched cli worker whose supervisor died still names no process, so that shape of the same defect stays open and needs its own node
